name: Eleazar Eleazer
overview: Eleazar, the son of Aaron, is established in Scripture as a key priestly figure who succeeded his father in the high priesthood, symbolized by the transfer of Aaron's garments to him before Aaron's death (Numbers 20:26). He was appointed chief over the Levites, overseeing the sanctuary and its sacred duties, including the management of the anointing oil, incense, and offerings (Numbers 3:32; 4:16). His role highlights the continuity of God’s covenantal priestly service through his lineage, as he also assisted Moses in the census and participated in the division of the Promised Land with Joshua.
